name: @projexlight/redis-runtime
summary: Redis client runtime — cluster-aware client, soft-cap counter, rate-limit primitives, distributed lock helpers. Every SDK that needs sub-ms cache or distributed coordination imports from here.

hooks.name: initRedis
hooks.description: Initialize the Redis client (cluster or single-node based on env).

hooks.name: closeRedis
hooks.description: Graceful shutdown — drain in-flight commands, exit clean.

hooks.name: withLock
hooks.description: Acquire a distributed lock for a duration; auto-release on callback exit.

hooks.name: tokenBucket
hooks.description: Rate-limit primitive — token-bucket counter on a key.

scenarios.title: Service initializes Redis on boot
scenarios.when_to_use: Every service that uses caching / rate-limits / locks.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Client connects to cluster or single-node based on REDIS_URL shape. Failed init refuses service boot.

scenarios.title: Cross-pod distributed lock for a once-per-tenant job
scenarios.when_to_use: Background worker that must not run concurrently across replicas — withLock ensures only one pod runs at a time.
scenarios.example_code:
import { withLock } from '@projexlight/redis-runtime';
await withLock(`tenant:${tenant_id}:rollup`, 60_000, async () => { /* ... */ });
scenarios.expected_outcome: Only one replica runs the inner block. Lock auto-releases on callback exit or TTL expiry.

scenarios.title: Per-tenant rate limit via token bucket
scenarios.when_to_use: Hosted MCP / API gateway need to cap per-tenant traffic; tokenBucket gives a fast Redis-backed counter.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Counter shared across all replicas in the cluster. Burst-tolerant + sustained-rate-limited.

compliance_posture.notes: TLS required for production. No PII cached — only counters + locks + ephemeral session data.
